messages:
Sam: Heads-up — saw a short latency spike on prod runtime during the 03:10 UTC window. Throughput dipped ~18%. p95 jumped from ~120ms -> ~460ms. Anyone on call?
Raj: I'm on it, grabbing profiler and logs.
Kevin: I suspect the batch heuristics change we rolled Tuesday (adaptive_merge). Could be keeping tiny batches that trigger a slower kernel path.
Li: Traces are thin around that time — looks like our sampling dropped a lot of fast-path traces. Only a couple KV-cache hit events recorded.
Nina: ops-bot shows autoscaler added pods at 03:11. Node 5 had transient CPU steal; noisy neighbor possible.
Tom: Pulled a CPU profile from node-5, reproducer attached. Hot loop in kernel_selector::pick_best that often picks fallback_int8 for batch_size <= 4.
Tom: ```
# profiler snippet
kernel_selector::pick_best(batch_size=3, seq_len=16) -> chosen_kernel=fallback_int8
latencies: fallback_int8=420us, fp16_fast=120us (expected)
```
Raj: fallback_int8 being slower here is new. Did quant profiles change recently? I remember optimize-service rolled quant_profile=v2 last week.
Kevin: Correct — quant_profile v2 altered the cost_model to favor int8 for locality. It inadvertently biases selection for small batches.
Li: Big observability gap: tracing sampling is 1% for successful requests. These were success responses so most outliers aren't captured. We need better sampling for generation endpoints.
Nina: Also dashboard p95 is computed from per-pod percentiles aggregated at ingestion. That can mask cross-pod spikes — we should compute global histograms instead.
Sam: Can we replay real requests from the CDS to validate the hypothesis?
ops-bot: Replayed 200 requests from 03:08-03:15 onto canary; when quant_profile=v2 + adaptive_merge enabled, canary p95 shows ~480ms.
Raj: Ok confirmed by replay. Hypothesis: adaptive_merge preserves small batches that, combined with the new quant cost_model, cause kernel_selector to choose fallback_int8 for many short chats. Fallback_int8 is slower for this micro-config.
Kevin: Short-term mitigation: revert adaptive_merge flag to previous behavior until we update the kernel_selector cost model. I'll open a revert PR and a rollback runbook.
Li: Short-term observability fixes: bump tracing sampling to 10% for generation APIs, and add a tag to capture `fast_path` vs `fallback` kernel choices so we collect kv-cache hit/miss counts.
Tom: Filed a metrics change to migrate p95 computation to global histograms (tdigest) at ingestion; also adding a short pipeline to backfill available raw samples for the 03:08-03:15 window.
Nina: Logs — our log-sampler dropped many low-latency events; raising log retention for generation pods and adding an indexing fallback. Filed INF-789 to track.
Sam: Postmortem plan: root cause is interplay between quant_profile v2 cost_model and adaptive_merge; observability blindspots (trace sampling + aggregated p95 + log sampling) slowed diagnosis. Action items below. Who owns what?
Raj: I'll own kernel_selector cost model updates and a test matrix for small-batch behavior.
Kevin: I'll revert adaptive_merge on prod and coordinate the deploy rollback.
Li: I'll push the tracing sampling config change and add the fast_path tag capture.
Tom: I'll land the histogram p95 ingestion change and backfill.
Nina: I'll drive the logs-sampling/resend ticket and validate we have raw indices for the window.
Sam: I'll write the incident summary and coordinate the postmortem.
ops-bot: Action items recorded: REVERT(adaptive_merge) -> assigned to Kevin; KERNEL_COST_MODEL -> Raj; TRACE_SAMPLING -> Li; HISTOGRAM_P95 -> Tom; LOGS_INDEX_FALLBACK -> Nina. ETA 48h for initial fixes. :thumbsup:
tracebot: Adding a note — captured canary replay artefacts saved to s3://redwood-incidents/1801234567/replay.tar.gz
Sam: Thanks everyone. Let's follow up in the postmortem doc with timelines and the mitigation checklist.
